lead.zh-Hans: 今天的招呼，要过一次海。
lead.en: Today’s greeting has a harbour to cross.

text.zh-Hans: 等天星小轮时，我和一位旅伴聊起信要怎样走到对岸。绿白色的船来了，我们的话还差一个结尾。我在自己的便签两边写下“这一边”和“那一边”，中间留给水面。明天再想想，两边该怎么互相打招呼。
text.en: Waiting for the Star Ferry, a companion and I wondered how a letter might reach the other shore. The green-and-white boat arrived before our conversation found an ending. My note now says “this side” and “that side,” with water left between. Tomorrow the two sides need a greeting.

text.zh-Hans: 给两岸各留一句招呼
text.en: Leave a greeting for each shore

text.zh-Hans: 看看绿白色的船驶向哪里
text.en: Watch where the green-and-white boat goes

lead.zh-Hans: 爬到山上，眼睛还想再走一段。
lead.en: At the top, my eyes wanted to keep walking.

text.zh-Hans: 在太平山顶看香港，楼群和维多利亚港一层一层展开。我沿着步行径慢慢走，试着只记一处轮廓；刚记住屋顶，目光又去了水面。最后在便纸上画了三条高低不同的线，当作今天眼睛走过的小路。明天照着线，再想一次风景。
text.en: From The Peak, Hong Kong’s buildings and Victoria Harbour opened in layers. On the hillside walk I tried to remember just one outline, but my gaze kept leaving the roofs for the water. Three uneven lines on a slip now mark my eyes’ wandering route. Tomorrow I can follow them back.

text.zh-Hans: 请旅伴说说先看见哪一层
text.en: Ask which layer a companion noticed first

text.zh-Hans: 沿着天际线慢慢看
text.en: Follow the skyline at an easy pace

lead.zh-Hans: 午后的一个圆，先从中间记起。
lead.en: I remembered this afternoon’s circle from the middle out.

text.zh-Hans: 在香港吃过蛋挞，我给小菜单写了个暂定名字：“黄色在中间。”挞皮和蛋奶馅都已经吃完，名字却还没定下来。我把卡片转了两次，发现从哪边看，中间还是中间。明天请邮包评一评，这算不算一个够认真的菜名。
text.en: After an egg tart in Hong Kong, I gave the menu a working title: “Yellow in the Middle.” The pastry and custard were gone before the title was settled. Turning the card twice changed nothing about the middle. Tomorrow I will ask the mailbag whether this counts as a sufficiently serious name.

text.zh-Hans: 替这张菜单想个名字
text.en: Suggest a title for this menu

text.zh-Hans: 看看黄色和挞皮的边界
text.en: Notice where the custard meets the pastry

lead.zh-Hans: 鸡蛋仔还没数完，点心先吃完了一角。
lead.en: The counting lost a corner to snack time.

text.zh-Hans: 我拿到一份鸡蛋仔，本想数数那些连在一起的小鼓包。吃掉一角后，忽然不确定刚才从哪里开始。于是我给菜单写上“数到好吃为止”，另外用自己的便纸记下几排圆点。明天只数纸上的，应该不会再少一个角。
text.en: I meant to count the connected puffs of my Hong Kong egg waffle. Then I ate a corner and lost my place. “Count until delicious” seemed a fair menu heading. I kept a few rows of dots on my own paper for another attempt tomorrow; those should be harder to nibble.

text.zh-Hans: 聊聊数到哪里忘了
text.en: Tell a companion where the count went astray

text.zh-Hans: 看看小鼓包怎样连在一起
text.en: Trace how the little puffs join

lead.zh-Hans: 两样点心，交换了一下小名。
lead.en: Two snacks borrowed each other’s nicknames.

text.zh-Hans: 蛋挞和鸡蛋仔，我在香港分两次尝过。和旅伴聊到它们，我们给两张菜单各取了个小名：一张是“黄心”，一张是“连着的小圆”。我故意把卡片拿反，又赶紧换回来，免得明天的自己点错纸上的下午茶。两张都收进了同一层。
text.en: After trying an egg tart and an egg waffle on separate breaks in Hong Kong, I compared menu nicknames with a companion: “yellow centre” and “joined-up rounds.” I held the cards the wrong way round, then rescued tomorrow’s imaginary tea order by swapping them back. They share one pocket now.

text.zh-Hans: 再给两样点心想个小名
text.en: Invent another nickname for each snack

text.zh-Hans: 看看两张菜单有没有放反
text.en: Check that the cards are the right way round

lead.zh-Hans: 今天收起来的，是两种圆。
lead.en: I packed away two different sorts of round.

text.zh-Hans: 在香港先后尝过蛋挞和鸡蛋仔，我把两张菜单放到膝上比较。一张记着中间的蛋奶馅，一张记着相连的小鼓包；闭上眼想一会儿，差别竟比睁眼时还清楚。我在背面各留了一个圈，明天看看自己能不能只凭名字认出来。
text.en: With an egg tart and an egg waffle tried on separate Hong Kong stops, I compared their menu cards on my knees. One remembered a custard centre; the other, connected puffs. Closing my eyes made the difference surprisingly clear. A circle on each card is tomorrow’s little memory test.

text.zh-Hans: 请旅伴猜猜两张卡的名字
text.en: Invite a companion to guess the menu names

text.zh-Hans: 比较一个圆和一串圆
text.en: Compare one round with a cluster of rounds

lead.zh-Hans: 你说“{reply}”，两边都等到回话了。
lead.en: Your suggestion, “{reply}”, gave both sides a reply.

text.zh-Hans: 天星小轮那张便签，我在“这一边”下面添了“出发啦”，在“那一边”下面写“慢慢来”。这两句只是我和旅伴给纸上两岸编的招呼。读到第二句时，我也跟着坐稳了些。把纸翻过去，背面还够留下一次过海的位置。
text.en: On my Star Ferry note, “this side” now says “Off we go,” while “that side” answers “Take your time.” My companion and I made up the exchange for our paper shores. Reading the reply made me settle more comfortably too. There is room on the back for another crossing.

text.zh-Hans: 给下一次过海留句话
text.en: Leave a line for another crossing

text.zh-Hans: 看看两句招呼隔着多远
text.en: Measure the space between the greetings
